description.content:
The Checkout Page seller API: checkout pages, events, forms, products, bookings, payments, subscriptions, customers, coupons, webhooks and more.

This collection is generated from the OpenAPI spec in the [Checkout Page developer tools repo](https://github.com/checkout-page/checkoutpage-api-sdk/tree/main/postman), so it covers the same API as the SDKs.

## Get an API key

1. Sign in to the [Checkout Page dashboard](https://checkoutpage.com/dashboard).
2. Go to **Settings** > **API keys** and generate a key. Copy it straight away: it is only shown once.
3. Set the `apiKey` variable to your key. Use the "Checkout Page" environment from the repo, or set it on your fork of this collection.

Every request sends the key in the `Authorization` header. The requests inherit this from the collection, so you only set it once.

## Test mode

A test API key only reads test data, and the records it creates are test records. Use one to try the API without touching live data.

Purchases made while a page is in test mode create test records with `livemode: false`, and no real money moves. A live key leaves test records out by default. Add `livemode=false` to a list or get request to read them with a live key. Write requests always use the mode of your API key.

## Variables

- `baseUrl`: the API host. Defaults to https://api.checkoutpage.com.
- `apiKey`: your API key. Keep it in an environment as a secret, and never share it.

## Learn more

- API reference: https://checkoutpage.com/docs
- SDKs, CLI and this collection: https://github.com/checkout-page/checkoutpage-api-sdk

Creates a checkout page together with its product and default fields in a single request.

Use this endpoint whenever you need to accept payments. It supports four payment flows, controlled by the `productData.price` object:

- **One-time payment** - set `price.amount` and `price.currency`. Do not set `price.recurring`, `price.paymentPlan`, or `price.payWhatYouWant`.
- **Pay What You Want (PWYW)** - set `price.payWhatYouWant: true`. `price.amount` becomes the minimum; leave it at `0` to allow free purchases. PWYW cannot be combined with subscriptions or payment plans.
- **Subscription (recurring)** - set `price.recurring` with `interval` (`day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`) and `intervalCount`. Optionally add `trialPeriodDays` or a `billingCycleAnchorConfig`.
- **Payment plan (installments)** - set `price.paymentPlan` with `interval`, `intervalCount`, and `planIterations` (the fixed number of payments after which the plan completes).

`price.recurring` and `price.paymentPlan` are mutually exclusive - set only one.

Default name and email fields are always created automatically. Pass `fields` to add extra checkout fields.

Creates an event booking without collecting card payment. The full booking flow runs: tickets are issued, a confirmation email with the ticket PDF is sent to the customer, live-mode bookings decrement ticket-type capacity, and booking webhooks fire. With a `paymentOption` the booking is recorded as `unpaid` and settled outside checkout via the chosen manual option (`invoice` or `cash_on_delivery`); a free booking simply has nothing due. With `complimentary: true` the booking is recorded as `paid` with `amount`, `amountPaid` and `amountDue` of 0 and `isComplimentary: true`, while the ticket lines keep their face value and `complimentaryDiscountAmount` records what they would have cost. Storefront rules are enforced: every required field on the event must be supplied, tickets must be enabled, on sale and in stock (a disabled ticket type, or any ticket in a disabled ticket group, cannot be booked, not even as a complimentary booking), and the event registration limit applies. Requires a connected Stripe account.
